Subject: Production timeouts across inference endpoints - urgent

Laura —

We started seeing a sharp increase in timeouts (client 504) and 5xx/429 errors on our inference routes beginning ~21:40 UTC. Our monitoring shows: 5xx rate peaked at ~8.3% and 429s hit ~12% for a sustained 22 minutes, and users experienced degraded UX (failed chat refreshes and embed batch failures). Retries on our side amplified the issue and caused downstream timeouts.

We believe this is customer-impacting and need immediate assistance: can you open an incident, confirm whether this is a Redwood service degradation, and provide any recommended mitigation (quick fallback model, route-level throttles, or bypass) while you investigate? I'm attaching a small sample of traces and a consolidated error log (server-logs-2027-10-08.zip) — happy to join a bridge.

This is impacting our end-users and our CS leadership is asking for a timeline and root cause.

— Aisha

Laura / team — initial triage notes from the bridge:

Summary of what we see so far:
- Traffic pattern: a traffic burst aligned with NewScale's nightly batch restart at ~21:36 UTC. Large fan-out of short-lived sessions resulted in many cold KV cache misses.
- Autoscaler: the burst_capacity policy for the tenant's dedicated pool had been inadvertently set to 0 by a recent config push (PR #3328). That meant we failed to spin up burst instances for ~3 minutes.
- Retry amplification: client retries from NewScale (10s retry window) pushed queued requests back into the runtime while cache repopulation was ongoing. Combined with a disabled burst pool this produced request queuing and 429 backpressure.
- Control plane: the fallback route selector had a race when preferred variant was overloaded — requests fell back to a heavier variant briefly increasing latency and timeouts.

Immediate mitigations applied (22:38–22:42 UTC):
- Re-enabled burst_capacity for NSC-894 pool (brought up 2 gpus).
- Applied a soft token-bucket limiter on the tenant route to flatten spikes (client-facing throttles for 60s).
- Adjusted route fallback policy to prefer fastest compatible variant to avoid expensive fallbacks.

Post-mitigation observations: 5xx/429 rates subsided within 4 minutes; by 22:46 UTC error rates returned to baseline.

Attachments: server-logs-2027-10-08.zip (from NewScale), mitigation-checklist.pdf (ops steps)

Proposed follow-ups (see detailed action list below):
1) Create a tenant-level runbook for burst events and cache-warm strategies (owner: dev@redwood.com, ETA: 2027-10-15).
2) Add an alert for sustained 429 rate >2% over 5m correlated with cache-miss rate >30% (owner: infra-alerting team, ticket JIRA-OPS-1214).
3) Patch autoscaler config validation to prevent burst_capacity=0 being merged for Dedicated tenants (owner: infra-config, ETA: 2027-10-12).
4) Recommend NewScale adopt an exponential backoff with jitter for client retries to avoid synchronized retries.
5) Run a synthetic load test replicating NewScale's restart pattern in staging, measure cache warm times and autoscaler latency (owner: perf eng).

We’ll log details to JIRA-OPS-1214 and follow up with a full postmortem.

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

- ALERTING: New composite alert for 429 spike correlated with cache-miss ratio (infra-alerts) — JIRA-OPS-1214 — ETA 2027-10-11.
- CONFIG VALIDATION: Block PRs setting burst_capacity <= 0 for Dedicated tenants (infra-config) — PR guard clause — ETA 2027-10-12.
- CLIENT GUIDANCE: Update onboarding docs for Dedicated customers to recommend exponential backoff with capped retries (DX Docs team) — ETA 2027-10-20.
- CAPACITY: Offer expedited Dedicated bump for impacted tenants; propose temporary reserve of 2 GPUs for NewScale for the next 30 days while we tune autoscaler (owner: sales+capacity ops) — action: Laura to confirm acceptance.
- SLO TUNING: Adjust SLO alarm thresholds to include 95th/99th latency in tenant pages and start alerting on sustained 429 > 2% over 5m (SRE/observability) — ETA 2027-10-18.

Ticket references: JIRA-OPS-1214 (alerting), JIRA-ENG-3348 (autoscaler guard), DOCS-592 (client retry guidance).

I’ll own the runbook and the initial patch for autoscaler validation; I’ll open the JIRA tickets and link them to the HubSpot deal.

Subject: Exec summary: NSC-894 incident (customer-impacting timeouts & 429 spike) and requested leadership commitments

Marcus / Hannah —

Quick executive summary from tonight’s NewScale incident (for context):
- Impact: Brief production outage window for NewScale customers caused by combined factors: autoscaler config (burst_capacity disabled), cache cold start at nightly job restart, and aggressive client retries. Visible symptoms were 5xx/429 spike between 21:36–21:46 UTC and elevated latencies.
- Immediate remediation: Dev re-enabled burst pool and applied temporary throttles; error rates returned to baseline in ~4 minutes.
- Customer impact: NewScale experienced failed chat refreshes and interrupted embedding jobs; CS reports loss of revenue for one customer segment during the window.

Requested leadership commitments:
1) Approve an expedited temporary Dedicated capacity reservation for NewScale (2 GPUs) for 30 days while we execute runbook and tuning. Sales is prepared to offer a partial discount; I propose we authorize a $50k credit against the commitment to maintain the relationship. (Decision needed by EOD 2027-10-10)
2) Prioritize autoscaler config guard (JIRA-ENG-3348) and alerting ticket (JIRA-OPS-1214) into the next sprint — attention from infra-config and infra-alerts leads required.
3) Approve a postmortem customer call tomorrow (Oct 10) with execs from both sides; Laura & Monica will present remediation and compensation.

I’ve attached the MAP and logs and linked JIRA tickets in the HubSpot record.

Next steps: Dev will deliver runbook draft by 2027-10-15; Monica to confirm MAP acceptance with NewScale; I will follow up on the capacity offer and credit approval.

Thanks — Laura
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
